question: How many audio control panels are installed on the flight deck?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

explanation: A panel at each of the captain, first officer and observer stations lets every occupant select transmitters and receivers independently.

question: What is the function of the mask and boom selector on the audio control panel?

options.text: It selects the alternate audio path to VHF 1
It selects between the flight interphone and the service interphone
It selects which microphone is live, the headset boom or the oxygen mask
It switches the audio between the headset and the flight deck speaker

explanation: After donning the oxygen mask the crew must still be able to transmit, and the selector routes the microphone accordingly.

question: What does the R/T position of the control wheel switch do?

options.text: It transmits on the radio selected on the audio control panel
It transmits on VHF 1 regardless of the panel selection
It keys the passenger address system
It connects the pilot to the cabin crew

explanation: The switch keys whichever transmitter the panel has selected, so mic selection is verified before transmitting.

question: What does the I/C position of the control wheel switch select?

options.text: The SELCAL decoder
The flight interphone between crew stations
The passenger address system
The service interphone to the ground crew

explanation: It gives an intercom path between the flight deck stations without transmitting on any radio.

question: What is the purpose of the alternate position on the audio control panel?

options.text: It routes all audio to the flight deck speaker
It transfers audio control to the other pilot panel
It provides a direct audio path to VHF 1, bypassing the normal audio system
It selects the standby frequency on the tuning panel

explanation: If the audio management system fails, the crew still has one usable radio through a hard wired path.

question: What do the voice, both and range filter selections control?

options.text: The volume balance between the headset and the speaker
Which VHF receiver is connected to the headset
The squelch level on the selected radio
Which part of a navigation aid audio signal is heard

explanation: Selecting the ident portion lets the crew confirm the station identifier without the voice broadcast masking it.

question: Why is the audio identifier of a navigation aid checked before use?

options.text: To confirm the correct station is tuned and is serviceable
To confirm the navigation display range is appropriate
To check the audio control panel filters are working
To verify the receiver volume is correctly set

explanation: A navaid can be tuned correctly yet be the wrong station or be transmitting while unserviceable, and the ident is the check for both.

question: How many VHF transceivers are fitted as standard?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

explanation: Two allows one to be used for control while the other is used for company or a second agency, with a third available as an option.

question: What does the transfer switch on a radio tuning panel do?

options.text: It transfers control of the radio to the other pilot
It switches the radio between VHF and HF
It selects the emergency frequency directly
It exchanges the active and standby frequencies

explanation: Preselecting the next frequency in the standby window means a change requires only one action at the moment it is needed.

question: What determines the usable range of a VHF transmission?

options.text: Line of sight between the aircraft and the station
The squelch setting on the receiver
The time of day and ionospheric conditions
The power output of the transmitter alone

explanation: Because the propagation is essentially straight line, range increases with altitude and is very limited at low level.

question: Why is HF used for oceanic and remote area communication?

options.text: It does not require a ground station
It is immune to atmospheric interference
Its sky wave propagation gives very long range
It provides a clearer signal than VHF at all ranges

explanation: Reflection from the ionosphere lets the signal travel far beyond line of sight, which is what makes it usable where no VHF coverage exists.

question: What is the purpose of SELCAL?

options.text: It automatically selects the best available frequency
It encrypts company communications
It records incoming transmissions for later replay
It allows a ground station to alert the crew without continuous listening watch

explanation: A coded call addressed to that airframe relieves the crew of monitoring a noisy HF channel for hours at a time.

question: How is a SELCAL call annunciated to the crew?

options.text: By a voice announcement on the flight deck speaker
By a chime and a light
By a message on the navigation display only
By a flashing master caution

explanation: The alert has to be noticeable without being alarming, since it indicates a routine call rather than a failure.

question: What does the flight interphone system connect?

options.text: The flight deck to the ground crew station
The flight deck to the cabin attendant stations
The flight crew stations to each other
The flight deck to the passenger address system

explanation: It is the internal circuit for the flight deck occupants, kept separate from the systems used to reach the cabin and the ground.

question: What does the service interphone system connect?

options.text: The flight deck stations to each other only
The cabin attendant stations to each other only
The passenger address amplifier to the cabin speakers
The flight deck to ground crew and service stations around the airplane

explanation: Maintenance and ground handling need a voice path at the jacks located around the airframe, which is what this system provides.

question: What is the effect of the service interphone switch on the overhead panel?

options.text: It powers the passenger address amplifier
It connects the external service jacks to the system
It transfers the flight interphone to the cabin
It silences the ground crew call horn

explanation: The jacks are normally isolated in flight so that an open circuit or a plugged in headset cannot interfere with crew communication.

question: Where does the horn sound when the flight deck calls the ground crew?

options.text: At the forward entry door
In the nose wheel well
At the refuelling panel
In the forward cargo compartment

explanation: The wheel well is where the ground crew headset station is located, so the alert is placed where the engineer will hear it.

question: How does the ground crew attract the attention of the flight crew?

options.text: By using the passenger address system
By switching the external power on and off
By operating a call switch that produces an aural and visual alert on the flight deck
By keying the service interphone twice

explanation: A dedicated call function avoids relying on someone already wearing a headset on the flight deck.

question: What happens when the attendant call switch is operated from the flight deck?

options.text: The cabin lights flash briefly
An announcement is broadcast over the passenger address system
The cabin interphone rings continuously until answered
A chime sounds in the cabin and a light illuminates at the attendant station

explanation: The combination of sound and light means the call is noticed even by a crew member away from the station.

question: Which source has the highest priority on the passenger address system?

options.text: The flight deck
Boarding music
The forward attendant station
Prerecorded announcements

explanation: In an emergency the flight crew announcement must override everything else, which is why the priority is built into the system rather than agreed procedurally.

question: How does the flight crew make a passenger address announcement?

options.text: By using the flight interphone with the speaker turned up
By pressing the attendant call switch twice
By selecting PA on the audio control panel microphone selector and keying the microphone
By selecting the service interphone and keying the microphone

explanation: The address system is treated as another transmitter selection on the panel, which keeps the interface consistent with the radios.

question: Which passenger address source has the lowest priority?

options.text: A prerecorded safety announcement
A flight deck announcement
A cabin crew announcement
Boarding music

explanation: Entertainment audio is the first thing interrupted, since anything else being broadcast carries more useful information.

question: What does the cockpit voice recorder record?

options.text: Radio transmissions only
Audio from each crew station and from the flight deck area microphone
The flight interphone and the passenger address only
Only the captain station audio

explanation: Recording both the individual stations and the ambient sound gives investigators the conversation and the environment it took place in.

question: What is the purpose of the flight deck area microphone?

options.text: It provides a backup transmitter if both boom microphones fail
It feeds the passenger address system during an evacuation
It monitors flight deck noise levels for maintenance purposes
It captures ambient sounds such as warnings, switch movements and unheadsetted speech

explanation: Much of what happens on a flight deck never passes through a headset, and the area microphone is what preserves it.

question: What is the typical recording duration of a modern solid state cockpit voice recorder?

options.text: Thirty minutes
One hour
Two hours
Twenty five hours

explanation: Solid state units record far longer than the older tape systems they replaced. Verify the duration fitted to your fleet.

question: Under what conditions can the cockpit voice recorder be erased?

options.text: On the ground with the parking brake set
In flight with both autopilots engaged
At any time from the flight deck
Only by maintenance with the recorder removed

explanation: The interlock exists so that a recording cannot be erased in flight or immediately after an event while the airplane is still rolling.

question: What is the purpose of the headphone jack on the recorder panel?

options.text: To connect a portable recorder for maintenance
To verify that the recorder is receiving audio during the test
To provide an additional listening station for the observer
To allow the crew to replay the previous flight

explanation: The test confirms the unit is actually capturing audio rather than simply being powered.

question: When does the cockpit voice recorder operate?

options.text: Only in flight, starting at liftoff
Only when the crew selects it before departure
Only when both engines are running
Automatically whenever electrical power is available under the normal operating conditions

explanation: Automatic operation removes any dependence on the crew remembering to start it, including during ground events.

question: With the airplane on battery power only, which communication radio remains available?

options.text: VHF 1
The HF radio
The passenger address system
VHF 2

explanation: Essential communication is preserved on a single radio fed from the battery powered bus. Verify the bus arrangement against your operator FCOM.

question: Why is 121.5 MHz monitored when a second radio is available?

options.text: It is the international emergency frequency used for distress and urgency calls
It is the frequency reserved for ground handling
It is the frequency used by SELCAL to address the aircraft
It is the standard company frequency in Europe

explanation: Maintaining a listening watch means a distress call or a relay request is heard even when the crew is working another frequency.

question: What is the advantage of a datalink communication system over voice?

options.text: It replaces the need for a cockpit voice recorder
Routine messages are exchanged without occupying a voice frequency or the crew attention
It provides longer range than HF in all conditions
It removes the need to monitor the emergency frequency

explanation: Written messages can be handled when workload permits and do not depend on a clear frequency at the moment they are sent.

question: How many transmitters can a crew member key at one time from a single audio control panel?

options.text: One
Two, one radio and one interphone
Two, if both are VHF
All selected transmitters simultaneously

explanation: A single microphone feeds a single selected transmitter, which is why an unintended selection means the message goes to the wrong agency.

question: Why is an audio control panel provided at the observer station?

options.text: Because the observer station has no headset jack otherwise
To allow the observer to control the passenger address priority
To provide a backup if a pilot panel fails
So that an additional occupant can monitor and transmit without using a pilot station

explanation: A check pilot or inspector needs to hear the operation and speak when required, without disturbing either operating pilot.
